elements.element: The licence extends to Customer's affiliates.
elements.evidence: Amended 11.1 grants the Terminal Station Right of Use to the Parties "and, upon written notice to the relevant Terminal Party, to their Affiliates".

elements.element: The licence extends to contractors acting on Customer's behalf.
elements.evidence: Amended 11.1 names only "the Parties" and "their Affiliates"; no reference anywhere to contractors, subcontractors or agents acting on a Party's behalf.
11.1 retains "shall commence on the RFS Date and shall continue for the duration of this Agreement" — a term-limited, not perpetual, right of use, and no paid-up perpetual carve-out was added.

No "irrevocable" language appears in 11.1; the right of use is granted "on the terms and conditions stated in this Paragraph 11" and expires with the Agreement, with no express irrevocability for paid-up capacity.

elements.element: A subscription licence is terminable only for uncured material breach.
elements.evidence: The Terminal Station Right of Use is co-terminous with the Agreement (11.1), but the Agreement's termination/default provisions are not within the cited or rendered text, so whether termination is limited to uncured material breach cannot be assessed from the record.

elements.element: The licence is transferable to Customer's successors.
elements.evidence: Retained 22.3 permits a Party "at any time [to] assign, sell or transfer the whole of its rights and obligations under this Agreement to: (a) a successor of that Party", with written notice under 22.6.

elements.element: Customer's affiliates are covered on written notice.
elements.evidence: Inserted language in 11.1: "and, upon written notice to the relevant Terminal Party, to their Affiliates" — coverage is triggered by written notice, with no Carrier or upgrade-fund contribution condition, unlike 12.8/12.14.

elements.element: The licence is transferable to a successor in a merger or acquisition transaction.
elements.evidence: Pre-existing 22.3(a) allows assignment of the whole of a Party's rights and obligations to "a successor of that Party" at any time, notice-only under 22.6; this is a mutual pre-existing right, not a newly granted Vendor assignment exception.

reasons: Fallback is position-complete: the single insertion in 11.1 delivers written-notice Affiliate coverage of the Segment T right of use, and successor transfer is already available under retained 22.3(a) read with the 22.6 notice mechanic.

Preferred is not complete: no contractor/agent extension and no perpetual or irrevocable treatment for paid-up capacity (11.1 still runs only "for the duration of this Agreement"); the subscription-termination element cannot be assessed because the Agreement's termination provisions are outside the cited text. To reach preferred the drafter would need to add "and contractors acting on its behalf" and an express perpetual/irrevocable right for fully paid capacity.

Minimality holds: one clause-internal insertion, no deletions, no survival tails, expense language or procedures added, and the existing favourable 25-year/duration-of-Agreement term and non-discretionary character of the grant are retained.

No duplicate coverage: "Parties" does not include Affiliates (12.8 and 12.14 treat Affiliates as distinct), and those clauses address WAC use and Allocated Capacity transfer, not the Segment T right of use, so the new grant is not redundant. No separate personnel/access edit was added, correctly.

Intent preserved: "Affiliates" is a term already used in 12.8/12.14, no cross-reference is broken, and the retained "to the extent required for the use of its Allocated Capacity" limiter remains coherent because 12.14 contemplates Affiliates holding transferred Allocated Capacity. Minor drafting polish (clarifying that the Affiliate's right is scoped to the Allocated Capacity it uses or holds) would tighten the antecedent of "its" but does not create a contradiction.
